papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Quantum Models for Time-series Forecasting
papers.what_it_is: A benchmarking study of five quantum models against classical forecasters on two real time-series data sets, run in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best classical models outperformed the best quantum models, and that the best found configurations of the classical models had a higher average accuracy than the best quantum models.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section V Conclusion, p.4
quotes: Overall we found that the best classical models outperformed the best quantum models.
The best found configurations of the classical models had a higher average accuracy than the best quantum models.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one benchmarking study on two data sets, noiseless simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The result covers univariate one-step forecasting on two data sets in simulation only.

assertions.value: The authors report that the relative performance of the models varied greatly with the data set, and that a quantum model offering improved performance for one data set does not imply a general advantage.
quotes: the relative performance of the models varied greatly depending on the data set, reinforcing the fact that a quantum model offering improved performance for one data set does not imply a general advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation from two data sets.

assertions.value: The authors state that they compared five quantum machine learning models with three classical approaches on two real data sets, that all quantum gate models were noiselessly simulated, and that simulated annealing was used for the quantum annealing model.
assertions.anchor: Section I Introduction and Abstract, p.1-2
quotes: we consider five different quantum machine learning models and compare them to three classical approaches for two real data sets.
All quantum gate models were noiselessly simulated and simulated annealing was used for the quantum annealing model.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup, Section I, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that forecasting a single time step for univariate data is one of the simplest prediction tasks, and that multidimensional input, multiple future time steps and evaluation on real quantum hardware are left for future work.
quotes: Forecasting a single time step for univariate data, which we considered in this work, is one of the simplest prediction tasks.
is left for future work, as is evaluating model performance on real quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits, Section V, p.4.

papers.title_in_file: Parametrized Quantum Circuit Learning for Quantum Chemical Applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, learning-curve and hardware results, Discussion, Conclusions; supplementary information not read.
papers.what_it_is: A study of 168 parametrized quantum circuits on two quantum-chemistry regression datasets, from state-vector simulation to a real IBM device.

assertions.value: The authors report that both PQC models were outperformed by their classical counterparts in model accuracy and in wall clock time to train and test.
assertions.anchor: Section 3 learning curves, p.22; Section 4 Discussion, p.27
quotes: both models are outperformed by their classical counterparts regarding both the wall clock time required to train and test the models and the accuracy of the models.
In general, both datasets are outperformed by their classical counterparts in terms of model accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on two datasets and the circuit families studied.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the ibm_quebec device the DDCC model gave train and test R2 of -0.6027 and -0.6013, and that state-vector simulation and the FakeQuebec noisy backend outperformed the real device.
quotes: both state-vector simulation and the FakeQuebec backend outperform the real device, where the ibm_quebec device provided a train and test R2 of -0.6027 and -0.6013, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware experiment on one device.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors attribute the loss of usefulness to hardware noise in their conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that none of the methods modeled the BSE49 dataset usefully, while for the DDCC water-conformer problem the best method reached R2 of approximately 0.60, rising to ca. 0.8 with more depth and training data.
quotes: none of the methods modeled the BSE49 dataset in a useful way
with R2 for the best method of approximately 0.60
which increased the R2 for the water conformers/DDCC problem to ca. 0.8
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from simulation on two datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study builds 168 PQCs from 14 data encoding strategies and 12 variational ansatze on circuits with 5 and 16 qubits, and that for other classes of PQCs not examined the trends may not hold.
quotes: We construct a comprehensive set of 168 PQCs by combining 14 data encoding strategies with 12 variational
circuits with 5 and 16 qubits
for other classes of PQCs, not examined in this study, these trends may not hold
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limit, Abstract and Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient Quantum Information-Inspired Ansatz for Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications to Atomic Systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, main-text results, hardware paragraphs and summary; supplementary material not read.
papers.what_it_is: A VQE ansatz built from von Neumann entropy and mutual information, tested on atomic ground-state energies in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that for up to 12 qubits in noiseless calculation the ansatz yields energies with 99.99% accuracy relative to the complete active space configuration interaction values, using only two blocks that contain at most 99% fewer 2-qubit gates than the UCC ansatz.
quotes: for up to 12 qubits (or 12 spin orbitals) noiseless calculation, the proposed ansatz yields energies with 99.99% accuracy relative to the complete active space configuration interaction values
while utilizing only two blocks, which contain at most 99% fewer 2-qubit gates than the UCC ansatz
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result on a set of atomic systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in terms of scaling, their ansatz requires a lower-order polynomial number of parameters than UCCSD and reduces the two-qubit gate count relative to UCCSD.
quotes: In terms of scaling, the number of parameters scales
the two-qubit gate count reduces from UCCSD's
assertions.certainty_reason: Scaling stated in the main text without a derivation there; supplementary not read.
assertions.reader_inference: The exact exponents are printed as superscripts in the paper (main text, p.5) and are not copied here.

assertions.value: The authors report that on IBM hardware the dominant group of Pauli terms reached an accuracy of 99.95% for P3+ and 99.99% for S4+ relative to the state-vector energy, while the second group reached only 13.37% for P3+ and 10.85% for S4+.
quotes: we obtain an accuracy of 99.95% for P3+ and 99.99% for S4+ on hardware with respect to the state-vector energy
we only obtain an accuracy of 13.37% for P3+ and 10.85% for S4+ relative to the state-vector energy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result for two atoms, with only two term groups measured.
assertions.reader_inference: Only two groups of terms were measured on hardware, so no full hardware energy accuracy is reported in these quotes.

assertions.value: The authors state that their noiseless simulations used the Qiskit 1.4.2 state-vector backend, and that hardware computations were performed for two atoms, P3+ and S4+.
quotes: All our noiseless simulations are carried out using Qiskit 1.4.2
Furthermore, we perform the quantum hardware computations of the two atoms, P3+ and S4+
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup, p.4-5.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Reinforcement Learning: Recent Advances and Future Directions
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section IX Future Directions and Open Problems, Section X Conclusion; the algorithm, architecture and application sections were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum reinforcement learning: frameworks, algorithms, architectures, SDKs, applications and open problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper is a survey of recent advances in quantum reinforcement learning to assess its potential in various applications.
quotes: In this survey, we investigate the recent advances in quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) to assess its potential in various applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that recent advances highlight the potential of VQC-based QRL to achieve quantum advantage even under noisy NISQ conditions, and that recent experimental findings further confirm quantum speedups in learning.
quotes: Recent advances highlight the potential of VQC-based QRL to achieve quantum advantage even under noisy NISQ conditions.
Recent experimental findings further confirm quantum speedups in learning, validating QRL for complex decision-making tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey's attribution of results to other work, with no study in this paper behind it.
assertions.reader_inference: Phrased as potential and attributed to cited work; the survey runs no experiment of its own.

assertions.value: The authors state that QRL faces challenges including algorithmic complexity, hardware limitations, and the lack of standardized tools and benchmarks.
assertions.anchor: Section X Conclusion, p.1 of the conclusion
quotes: However, QRL still faces several challenges. These include algorithmic complexity, hardware limitations, and the lack of standardized tools and benchmarks.
assertions.certainty_reason: An authors' assessment of the field.

assertions.value: The authors state that, unlike QML, QRL suffers from a lack of specialized SDKs, curated datasets, and standardized benchmarks.
assertions.anchor: Section IX Future Directions and Open Problems, item 2
quotes: Unlike QML, QRL suffers from a lack of specialized SDKs, curated datasets, and standardized benchmarks.
assertions.certainty_reason: An authors' assessment of the field.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Optimizers for Qumode State Preparation with Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, setup, results for Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, Conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of classical optimizers for preparing qumode target states with variational quantum algorithms.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Powell optimizer was exceptionally robust against sampling errors, and that the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation optimizer was distinguished for its efficiency and ability to handle increased parameter dimensionality.
quotes: the Powell optimizer was found to be exceptionally robust against sampling errors
the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation optimizer was distinguished for its efficiency and ability to handle increased parameter dimensionality effectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors report that in ideal simulations the Gaussian states were approximated within three layers, sampling simulations needed more layers, and the Non-Gaussian state needed up to 10 layers.
quotes: In ideal simulations, both Local and Non-local Gaussian states were effectively approximated within three layers.
The preparation of Non-Gaussian states proved more challenging, necessitating up to 10 layers to minimize the state preparation error effectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result for the tested states.

assertions.value: The authors report that in a sampling simulation of Gaussian-state learning all optimizers yielded final infidelity values of only 0.11 and 0.13 for 3 layers, and that convergence requires more than 3 layers.
assertions.anchor: Section IV.C Gaussian state, sampling simulation, p.4
quotes: all optimizers yield final infidelity values of only 0.11 and 0.13 for 3 layers. Hence, achieving convergence in sampling simulation for learning Gaussian states requires more than 3 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the bosonic systems were truncated to a 10-level system for general experiments, and that the tests covered different target states, ideal and sampling simulations, and varying numbers of basis gate layers.
quotes: we truncate the bosonic systems to a 10-level system for general experiments
including different target states, both ideal and sampling simulations, and varying numbers of basis gate layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Computing for Optimizing Aircraft Loading
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Background, QPU experiment results on Aria and Forte, Conclusions; algorithm derivation sections skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: An IonQ and Airbus study of a multi-angle layered variational algorithm for aircraft cargo loading, run on IonQ Aria and Forte QPUs.

assertions.value: The authors report that their experiments obtained the optimal solutions for all the problem instances studied, ranging from 12 qubits to 28 qubits, on IonQ QPUs Aria and Forte.
quotes: Our experiments obtain the optimal solutions for all the problem instances studied ranging from 12 qubits to 28 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on small instances from authors affiliated with the hardware vendor.
assertions.reader_inference: Two authors-lists affiliations are IonQ, the vendor of the hardware used.

assertions.value: The authors describe a proof of principle that found the optimal solution for choosing from up to 7 containers of 3 different size types for loading into 4 cargo slots, and state that solving many more containers and slots will be required to be of practical value.
quotes: In a proof of principle demonstration we found the optimal solution for choosing from up to 7 containers of 3 different size types for loading into 4 cargo slots.
To be of practical value the ability to solve for many more containers and slots will be required.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scale of its demonstration and its own limit, Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the Aria QPU instances the problems were optimized using the Qiskit Aer simulator and the optimal parameters were then used to initialize the circuit that was executed on the QPU.
quotes: These problem instances were optimized using the qiskit Aer simulator and the final optimal parameters were determined.
The optimal parameters were used to initialize the quantum circuit which was then executed on the Aria QPU
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental procedure.
assertions.reader_inference: For these instances the QPU sampled a circuit whose parameters were trained in simulation, which limits what the QPU result shows about hardware training.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, overview, statement of Theorem 6.1; the proofs and appendix were not read line by line.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper giving a quantum recommendation-system algorithm with polylogarithmic running time in the matrix dimensions, under a low-rank assumption and a quantum-accessible data structure.

assertions.value: The authors present a quantum algorithm for recommendation systems with running time O(poly(k)polylog(mn)), and prove that for most users the expected running time of Algorithm 6.1 is O(polylog(mn)poly(k)).
quotes: we present a quantum algorithm for recommendation systems that has running time O(poly(k)polylog(mn)).
the expected running time of Algorithm 6.1 is O(polylog(mn)poly(k)).
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 6.1, p.18, proved for a subset of users under the stated assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The bound holds under the low-rank assumption and quantum access to a classical data structure. Later classical work (Tang, 2018) is known to the reader and not in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm assumes a classical data structure to which quantum queries can be made, and that beyond the low-rank approximation assumption they make no additional assumptions about the classical data.
quotes: it assumes that there exists a classical data structure to which we can make quantum queries.
we do not make any additional assumptions about the classical data beyond the low rank approximation assumptions made by classical recommendation systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its model and assumptions, Section 1.1, p.5.

assertions.value: The authors claim this is the first algorithm for recommendation systems that runs in time polylogarithmic in the dimensions of the matrix, and state that all known classical algorithms that reconstruct an approximation of the preference matrix run in time polynomial in the matrix dimension.
quotes: All known classical algorithms for recommendation systems that work through reconstructing an approximation of the preference matrix run in time polynomial in the matrix dimension.
This is the first algorithm for recommendation systems that runs in time polylogarithmic in the dimensions of the matrix
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority and comparison claim made as of 2016; classical comparison not proved here.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to reconstruction-based classical algorithms known in 2016.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Eigensolvers in the Era of Distributed Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Conclusions; supplementary sections skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a VQE ansatz for a two-module distributed quantum architecture with a few inter-module operations.

assertions.value: The authors report from simulation that, for a dual-core VQE ansatz, three inter-module operations provide a significant advantage over no inter-module operations, and that three inter-QPU gates were sufficient for a significantly better ground-state approximation in all cases studied.
quotes: we show that three inter-module operations provide a significant advantage over no inter-module (or serially executed) operations.
In all cases studied, we found that three judiciously placed inter-QPU gates were sufficient to produce a significantly better approximation to the ground state energy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result for a few Hamiltonians.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study systems with up to 12 qubits and that their comparison is based on simulations and therefore limited to a small number of qubits.
assertions.anchor: Results and Conclusions, p.3 and p.5
quotes: We study systems with up to 12 qubits
Our comparison is based on simulations, and it is therefore limited to a small number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit, Conclusions, p.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that important questions remain open, including the impact of noise and the imperfect nature of interconnects.
quotes: A number of important questions remain open, including the impact of noise and the imperfect nature of interconnects.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit, Conclusions, p.5.
